title: Rate-limit-triggered route downgrade sending customer to compatible variant
creator: Asha Patel
description: Several production customer reports indicate requests are being downgraded to a 'compatible' quantized model variant in a different region when tenant-specific rate limits are tripped on the primary hosted pool. This causes higher latency, degraded text quality, and costly cross-region egress. Root cause appears related to the policy-evaluation path that executes during rate-limit enforcement: instead of returning a throttled error or queueing for local burst capacity the router selects the first compatible fallback that matches the policy set, which in some cases is a regionally-incompatible variant. The behavior surfaced across Hosted and Dedicated customers with mixed routing configs and led to two SEV-level escalations from enterprise customers.
impact: Customer-facing degradation: increased latency (avg +450ms), lower output fidelity (reported by 3 customers), unexpected cross-region egress charges. Affected ~0.2% of requests during peak windows; for impacted tenants spike to ~8% requests over a 30-minute window. Two enterprise escalations opened (CS-4341, CS-4379).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create tenant routing policy that prefers hosted pool eu-west-1 with model variant m-turbo-quantized-8bit as primary and compatible m-turbo-quantized-4bit in other regions as fallback.
2) Configure tenant rate limit low (e.g., 50 r/s) and enable burst policies that prefer local dedicated capacity for short bursts.
3) Generate traffic at a rate that triggers rate-limit enforcement on hosted pool (simulate 3x sustained rates).

4) Observe router decision logs: when rate limit triggers, router selects first compatible fallback variant without honoring regional affinity, leading to requests routed to us-east-1 compatible variant.
5) Confirm increased latency and quality delta via Golden prompt set and token-level latency traces in Console > Traces.
mitigation: Temporary mitigation applied: 1) increased tenant rate limit for affected customers, 2) pushed routing rule override that pins fallbacks to same-region variants, 3) activated denylist rule for cross-region compatible variants for impacted tenants. Mitigations reduced customer errors within 20 minutes. Long-term fix required in policy-evaluation precedence and rate-limit path.
proposed_fix: Change routing policy evaluation to return an explicit "RATE_LIMITED" decision when local pool is rate-limited and the tenant has no cross-region fallback consent. Modify fallback comparator to prefer same-region variants and respect tenant-level 'avoid-cross-region-failover' flag. Add a circuit-breaker that prevents automatic cross-region downgrade under rate-limit-induced paths unless explicit routing policy allows it.
implementation_notes: - Router module: add RateLimitDecision enum branch and thread-safe flag for short-circuiting fallback comparator.
- Policy engine: evaluate tenant-level attributes before scanning global compatible-variants index.
- Add a new unit test matrix covering (rate-limited local pool) x (tenant allow_cross_region true/false) x (fallbacks available).
- Update telemetry to emit 'rate_limit_routed_fallback' tag on traces and increment a new metric routing.rate_limit_fallback.count.
- Add e2e canary in staging: simulate heavy load and ensure no cross-region routing occurs for tenants with cross-region disallowed.
- Rollout plan: feature flag default-off; enable in limited DCs; monitor metric and customer tickets for 48h before full rollout.
